transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-16
Start: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Alex Kim (Redwood CSM); Connor O'Neill (EdgeWave CTO), Priya Desai (EdgeWave DevOps), Luis Martinez (EdgeWave Security), Hannah Cole (EdgeWave SRE)

Auto-summary: quick status: VPC peering established but intermittent route flaps; runtime upgrade in staging, some regressions in 95th/99th percentiles; security questions mostly answered but need KMS details and audit log retention numbers.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, um we'll do the usual sync — I have Maya and Alex from Redwood here too. Connor, Priya, you still good on time?
[00:08] Connor: yep, good to go. thanks Jordan.
[00:12] Maya: hi all, quick agenda — networking updates, routing/fallback checks, runtime upgrade status, bench highlights, then actions.
[00:18] Priya: sounds good. we got a couple of network flaps yesterday so hoping to dig into that.
[00:23] Jordan: cool, Priya — can you summarize current VPC peering state?
[00:27] Priya: yeah so peering is up between our VPC and the Redwood Private control plane, we saw a couple of route propagations not sticking — looks like a transient BGP session dropout on our side, um traced to a misconfigured route map, we pushed a fix last night. since then traffic looks stable but we did see a 30s blackhole during one of the heavier shot tests.
[00:46] Hannah: right, the blackhole coincided with a spike in concurrent open connections during the integration test, we had TCP retries and it ballooned the tails.
[00:58] Maya: thanks — that's consistent with the metrics we saw. on the Redwood side the control plane retried and we fell back to the regional gateway, which is expected, but it added ~250ms for affected requests.
[01:12] Jordan: okay, so we need to tighten the BGP timers and add a more aggressive health-check for the peering to failover quicker. Maya, did we already push the health-check patch to staging?
[01:21] Maya: yes, it's in staging in the v0.9 runtime image — healthcheck interval down to 10s and quicker route withdraw. we're seeing faster failovers in our sim, but we haven't run the full EdgeWave workload there yet.
[01:35] Connor: is v0.9 the runtime upgrade you mentioned last week? I thought the release had some performance fixes but also a couple of regressions?
[01:44] Maya: correct — v0.9 includes improved KV-cache warming and cheaper kernel paths for attention scoring, but we saw an unexpected tail latency regression under a specific token distribution — basically long prefix-heavy requests triggered more cache misses.
[02:00] Priya: can you explain that in lay terms? when we hit the model with long context prompts we saw slow responses?
[02:05] Maya: yeah, long context prompts cause larger KV entries and when the cache eviction policy struggles we get more CPU/GPU syncs which cause the long tails. so on small requests it's fine, but at 95th/99th it spikes.
[02:18] Luis: ok, from security perspective the peering outage is concerning — did any logs show failed auth or dropped packets we should worry about?
[02:26] Alex: we've captured the control plane logs and handed over the session traces to Priya's team. no auth failures, it appears network-only. we'll include packet captures in the shared folder.
[02:36] Jordan: perfect. on audit side, Luis — you had a few remaining questions about KMS and log retention?
[02:42] Luis: yeah, we need plaintext around the KMS key lifecycle, rotation schedule, HSM usage, and retention for admin audit logs — specifically 7 years for certain artifacts per our compliance team.
[02:55] Jordan: understood, we'll share the KMS/HSM whitepaper and confirm retention capabilities. Maya, can you pull retention numbers?
[03:02] Maya: yes, we can support configurable retention up to 10 years for audit logs with log export to S3 in the Private deploy; I'll get exact S3 lifecycle configs.
[03:11] Priya: thanks. back to performance — Connor, we ran a 10k/day token load test and saw average latency within SLA but tails were off. we'll post the CSVs.
[03:22] Connor: I reviewed the sheet — average 70ms but 99th was 1.3s, which is higher than acceptable for our chat use-case.
[03:31] Maya: two things to try: 1) increase the KV cache size and change eviction to LRU with sticky prefixes for your workload, 2) adjust batch sizing so that long-context requests don't block short ones — we have a config that separates by prefix length.
[03:47] Priya: what's the memory hit if we bump KV cache? we're constrained on the nodes.
[03:52] Maya: approximate hit is +15% RAM for a 30% larger cache, but that dramatically reduces misses in long-context flows. another option is to use the offload feature in v0.9 to spill cold KV pages to fast NVMe which keeps memory footprint lower but adds ~30ms on miss.
[04:09] Hannah: do we have NVMe on the current pilot nodes?
[04:12] Priya: not yet, it's on the checklist for next week's infra changes.
[04:16] Jordan: ok, so short-term we try cache tuning, medium-term we enable NVMe offload in a controlled window. Maya, can you give concrete knob values for Priya to test?
[04:25] Maya: yes — I'll push a sample config: kv_cache_size: 30% (from 20%), eviction: LRU, prefix_stickiness: true, and batch_max_tokens: 2048 with a separate queue for >4096 tokens.
[04:36] Priya: sounds good. we'll test that on staging.
[04:39] Connor: also want to revisit routing policy — you mentioned earlier fallback to regional gateway, but can we policy-route sensitive traffic to dedicated nodes to avoid noisy neighbor latency?
[04:49] Maya: absolutely — Redwood Private supports route tags and capacity pools, we can pin certain customer routes to dedicated capacity. that'll eliminate noisy neighbor interference at the cost of reserved capacity.
[05:00] Connor: what's the cost delta roughly?
[05:03] Jordan: rough math — reserved capacity for your profile adds about 25-40% to per-token cost but gives consistent 99th latency. we can model exact numbers after we see steady-state token volumes.
[05:15] Luis: from security, pinning routes to dedicated nodes requires us to verify isolation and multi-tenancy controls. do we get per-node audit and tenant separation proofs?
[05:24] Maya: yes, we'll provide isolation docs and auditing hooks; on Private you can enable per-route observability and export traces to your Splunk/Datadog.
[05:33] Priya: quick question — when you say "pin to dedicated capacity", is that a model-level pin or route-level?
[05:39] Maya: route-level, so you can keep model variants pooled. it's policy-driven.
[05:43] Connor: great. next item — benchmark anomaly where 99th jumped after large spike, is that reproducible?
[05:50] Maya: partially reproducible; our sim shows it under bursty startup patterns where warmup hasn't filled the KV. we recommend a warmup traffic pattern during deploys to prime caches.
[05:59] Priya: can we script that? we want an automated warmup step in CI/CD before switching traffic.
[06:04] Alex: yes, Redwood provides a warmup script example; we'll drop it in the shared repo.
[06:10] Jordan: ok, action for Maya to drop warmup script and tuned config. Priya to run perf test with those changes.
[06:16] Maya: will do.
[06:18] Luis: a security note — the warmup script will generate tokens and logs. we need to ensure it doesn't leak PII or keys; please provide a sanitized example.
[06:26] Maya: absolutely — sanitized by default.
[06:29] Priya: networking again — we saw intermittent MTU blackholes when jumbo frames were enabled on our side but not on the Redwood gateway, caused fragmentation issues. we disabled jumbo frames during the test and the issue stopped.
[06:42] Maya: ah, that explains some packet retransmits we saw. we'll add an MTU check as part of the peering checklist document.
[06:49] Jordan: good. on the compliance ask, Luis, you asked about 7-year retention — we can support long-term retention via log export; we'll send a doc that outlines retention + S3 lifecycle configs.
[06:59] Luis: thanks. also want to capture who owns the cert renewals for the peering endpoints.
[07:05] Priya: we do on our side, Redwood owns the control plane certs, we'll exchange a cert rotation schedule.
[07:12] Maya: one more note — there was a small mismatch in the model variant mapping in the routing table, looks like for a small subset of routes the fallback mapped to an older quantized model which increased latency. we fixed that mapping in staging yesterday.
[07:26] Connor: ok, so final list for this week?
[07:29] Jordan: summarize — Maya to share tuned config, warmup script, and KMS retention numbers; Jordan to share network diagram and peering checklist plus packet captures; Priya to run perf tests and confirm NVMe readiness; Luis to provide compliance question list; Alex to upload the CSVs and traces to the shared drive.
[07:46] Alex: I'll upload after this call and ping the thread.
[07:50] Priya: quick scheduling note — we're targeting an infra upgrade window Dec 29 for NVMe and runtime v0.9 canary, want Redwood on standby.
[07:59] Jordan: noted — we'll make sure an SE is on call.
[08:03] Connor: one last question — any blocker from Redwood side to do a controlled canary on Dec 29?
[08:09] Maya: no blockers, just need confirmation of network maintenance window and an agreed rollback plan.
[08:16] Jordan: ok we'll draft a rollback playbook and post by EOD Dec 18.
[08:22] Hannah: thanks, that's really helpful.
[08:25] Jordan: ok folks, appreciate the time. quick recap in the calendar invite and we'll follow up in the thread.
[08:31] Connor: thanks everyone.
[08:32] End meeting.

Notes on transcript quality: automatic speech-to-text had some errors around product names (e.g., "KV cache" as "K V cash") and some punctuation, cleaned minimally for readability.

- Redwood (Jordan/Maya): share network diagram, peering checklist, tuned configs, warmup script, KMS/HSM retention details by 2026-12-18/20.
- EdgeWave (Priya/Connor): run the perf tests with tuned config, validate NVMe availability, post results by 2026-12-22.
- Security (Luis): finalize compliance Qs and confirm retention needs by 2026-12-21.
- Schedule: tentative infra upgrade/canary for 2026-12-29 (rollback plan to be drafted).

End of transcript.
